statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-87697 (GHSA-c27m-942f-rcfh) is a .NET remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF): XPS synthetic hyperlinks exposed through UI Automation can bypass the restrictive navigation checks and reach attacker-controlled content after user interaction. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64 as the only affected .NET 10 packages, from 10.0.0 through 10.0.12, fixed in 10.0.13 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c27m-942f-rcfh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/471, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.13/10.0.13.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 264 packages of the twelve published builds (10.0.2-r0 through 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No WPF runtime code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder, UIAutomation, wpfgfx, PresentationNative or PenImc assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack; the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Ref and Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Internal nupkg files in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts hold only package metadata. The WPF-related files that are present are the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade with no WPF code; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml and System.Xaml.xml) in the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense package in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which hold no code; the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, which carries libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) and no WPF assembly; MSBuild props and targets in the Microsoft.Private.Winforms nupkg; and the Windows desktop SDK (Microsoft.NET.Sdk.WindowsDesktop), in the .NET SDK held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap and as a nupkg in dotnet10-runtime-artifacts, whose only assembly is the PresentationBuildTasks XAML build task with its resource assemblies. PresentationBuildTasks compiles none of the source files that the WPF changes between the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.112 and v10.0.113 source tags modify (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/compare/v10.0.112...v10.0.113); those files are in PresentationCore, PresentationFramework, ReachFramework, System.Xaml, DirectWriteForwarder and the wpfgfx native library. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. So the vulnerable WPF code is not in this owner.

CVE-2026-87697 (GHSA-c27m-942f-rcfh) is a .NET remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF): XPS synthetic hyperlinks exposed through UI Automation can bypass the restrictive navigation checks and reach attacker-controlled content after user interaction. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App runtime packs for Windows (win-x64, win-x86, win-arm64) as the affected .NET 8 packages, from 8.0.0 through 8.0.31, fixed in 8.0.32 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c27m-942f-rcfh, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/471, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.32/8.0.32.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux (linux-musl) from Microsoft's source release. Scanned all 220 packages of the ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder or wpfgfx assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. The WPF-related files that are present are the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB or smaller) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade that redirects a few types to other .NET libraries and contains no WPF code; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml, System.Xaml.xml and ReachFramework.xml) in a reference package, which describe the APIs and hold no code; and the Windows desktop transport nupkg, which carries only libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs and System.Diagnostics.EventLog) and no WPF code. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file (every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly with a CLR header), and none contains a Windows runtime pack. WPF is built only for Windows, so this owner does not contain the WPF component at all.
